1.note: Yahweh is using the formula **For three transgressions of …, and for four** throughout this chapter as a traditional Hebrew poetic device meaning complete or overflowing guilt. It does not mean a literal count of four specific sins. The number three shows a full measure, and the fourth pushes past the limit to trigger God’s judgment. If this would not be clear to your readers, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [For all the many wrong things Moab has done]

Here, **Moab** represents the people who live there. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [of the people who live in Moab]
The pronoun **it** refers to Yahweh’s decision to punish. Alternate translation: [I will not reverse my decision to punish]
The pronoun **his** refers to Moab, that is, to the people of Moab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [because of Moab’s burning]

In this culture, to burn someone’s bones was a terrible insult to the person. It involved violating his grave, and the burning was thought to disturb the person’s peace in the afterlife. You could include this information in a footnote if that would be helpful to your readers.

By **to lime**, Yahweh means that the king of Edom’s bones were burned so completely that they turned to white ashes. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [to white ashes]

2.note: Yahweh is speaking of fire completely destroying the citadels in Moab’s capital city, Kerioth, as if it would **devour** them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it will completely destroy the citadels of Kerioth]
**Moab** represents the people of Moab. Alternate translation: [and the people who live in Moab will die]

A **shofar** is a kind of horn, made from the horn of a ram, that people blew to give signals in battle. If your readers would not be familiar with what a shofar is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [with the blast of a signal horn]

3.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of removing this ruling judge of Moab as if he **will cut off** this ruler like a person would cut a branch off of a tree. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will remove the judge]
The pronoun **her** refers to Moab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [from the midst of Moab]

4.note: See how you translated these same phrases in [2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [For all the many wrong things Judah has done]

Here, **Judah** represents the people who live in the kingdom of Judah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [of those who live in Judah]
See how you translated the phrase **I will not turn it back** in [2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [I will not reverse my decision to punish]

Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean the **law of Yahweh** since he himself gave it to the people of Judah. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the law that Yahweh commanded them]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh** and **his**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [my law, and they did not keep my statutes]

Yahweh is speaking of the false gods that the people of Judah worshiped as if they were **lies**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their idols]

Yahweh is speaking of their being deceived into disobeying God’s laws as if they were being physically **led** to go the wrong way or **astray**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [deceived them]

It might seem that the expression **which their fathers walked after them** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [which their fathers walked after]

The pronoun **which** refers to the **lies**, or the false gods that Judah followed, that were mentioned in the previous line. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the false gods]
Here, **fathers** represents “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [their forefathers]

Yahweh is speaking of Judah’s devotion and service to idols as if they physically **walked after** them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [had faithfully served]

5.note: Yahweh is speaking of fire completely destroying the citadels in the capital of Judah, Jerusalem, as if it would **devour** them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it will completely destroy the citadels of Jerusalem]

6.note: See how you translated these same phrases in [2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [For all the many wrong things Israel has done]
Here, **Israel** represents the people of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the Israelites]
See how you translated the phrase **I will not turn it back** in [2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [I will not reverse my decision to punish]

Yahweh is using the adjective **righteous** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [those people who are righteous]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. He means that people in Israel are also selling **the needy** for a pair of sandals. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and their selling the needy]

Yahweh is using the adjective **needy** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and those people who are in need]

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that **a pair of sandals** would only cost a very small amount. This means that they sold needy people into slavery for a price as low as the price of a pair of sandals. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for as little as the price of a pair of sandals]

7.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the people of Israel oppressing and mistreating the poor as if they were **trampling on the head of the poor to the dust of the earth**, crushing them underfoot into the ground. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [cruelly oppressing the poor as if they are crushing their heads into the dust]

Yahweh is speaking of the denying justice to afflicted people as if they would **turn aside** from the **way** along which they should walk. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they deny justice to the afflicted]

Yahweh is referring to sexual relations in a polite way by using the phrase **go to**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [and a man and his father have sexual relations with the same girl]

Yahweh is using the adjective **afflicted** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [afflicted people]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **name** that is characterized by **holiness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my holy name]

Here, **the name of my holiness** represents Yahweh himself, who is holy. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me, Yahweh, who is holy]

8.note: The expression **taken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [garments that they took as pledges]
Yahweh is speaking of the temple as if it were a **house** in which he lived. Alternate translation: [in the temple]

Yahweh is not using this possessive form **their God** to indicate that the Israelites possess or control Yahweh but rather to emphasize that Yahweh is the God that the Israelites worship. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the God whom they worship]

9.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I destroyed** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that the Israelites could not have destroyed the Amorites without him but rather, he was the one who did it. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [It was I who destroyed]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **Amorite**. He means the Amorite people group in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Amorites]

Yahweh is using **from their faces** as a common expression of the culture to mean “on behalf of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [on their behalf]

The point of this comparison is that just as **cedars** are very tall, so the Amorite people were very tall. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [who was extremely tall, as cedar trees are]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the oaks** are very strong, so the Amorite people were very strong. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and he was very strong, as oak trees are]

Yahweh is continuing the comparison of the Amorites to trees and referring to all of the Amorite people by naming two extremes, **fruit from above** and **roots from beneath**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [them entirely, leaving no survivors]

10.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I brought** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he was the one who brought the people of Israel up from Egypt. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [It was I who brought you]

Even though Yahweh has been speaking about the people of Israel with third person pronouns, here he switches to speaking directly to them much more personally in the second person as **you**. This is a plural pronoun if your language marks that distinction. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make that clear. Alternate translation: [I brought you Israelites up]

11.note: Yahweh is speaking of choosing certain young men to become prophets and Nazirites as if they were objects that he would physically lift or **raise up** into a high position. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I chose]
The word **your** is plural here and throughout this passage because Yahweh is addressing the people of Israel, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and I raised up from your young men as Nazirites]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that what he has just said is true. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [This is surely so, sons of Israel!]

Amos is interjecting the phrase **the declaration of Yahweh** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

12.note: Yahweh assumes that readers will know that a Nazirite would have vowed not to drink wine according to rules laid out in Numbers 6:2-4. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [But you made the Nazirites break their vows and drink wine]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [you commanded them that they should not prophesy]

The term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly since **commanded** already includes that information.

13.note: Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus the Israelites’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you could use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Consequently]

13.q: מֵעִ֖יק תַּחְתֵּי⁠כֶ֑ם כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֤ר תָּעִיק֙ הָ⁠עֲגָלָ֔ה הַֽ⁠מְלֵאָ֥ה לָ֖⁠הּ עָמִֽיר
13.note: The point of this comparison is that just as load of sheaves of grain is heavy and presses down a cart so it can barely move, so Yahweh will press down heavily on the people of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [am pressing down on you heavily so you cannot escape just as a cart is pressed down and cannot move when its load of sheaves is too heavy]

14.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **retreat**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And the swift will not be able to flee]

Yahweh is using the adjectives **swift** and **strong** as nouns to mean certain kinds of people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with a equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [from the swift person and the strong person]

Yahweh is using the adjective **mighty** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and the mighty person]

15.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific person described as **the one grasping the bow**. He means archers in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and archers]

Yahweh is using the adjective **swift** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and the one who is swift on his feet]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific person described as **the one riding the horse**. He means horsemen in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and those riding horses]

16.note: Yahweh is using **the strong of his heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “courageous.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the most courageous]

Yahweh is using the adjective **mighty** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [among the mighty warriors]

In this context, **naked will he flee**, means that this mighty warrior ran away without any of his weapons and armor. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [he will flee stripped of his weapons and armor]

The phrase **in that day** refers to that time when Yahweh will punish them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at the time when I punish you]
See how you translated the phrase **the declaration of Yahweh** in 2:11.
